truth_boundary: This registry is the SINGLE source of truth for admin navigation. AdminLayout renders from it and the redirect framework reads from it. It declares BOTH the current state and the target state on purpose: the sidebar is not cut to the target until C13, because prompt section 2.5 forbids retiring a legacy route before parity, redirect, deep-link preservation, data preservation, navigation tests and documentation are all demonstrated. A registry that only described the target would make the gap invisible.

legacy_redirects.blocker: C13 verified: the blocker text ("Pipeline replacement lands in C3") was stale — C3 built the Pipeline workspace. The real problem is different. AdminDeals reads DEALS, a hard-coded array in src/lib/deals.js, and offers "Edit deal metadata and status" over a compile-time constant: there is no persistence at all. A deal catalogue is also not a pipeline, so /admin/pipeline is the wrong destination. Same class as the Benchmarks claim — the claim must be corrected before the route is retired, and the destination re-chosen.

C13 verified: the blocker text was stale. The real finding is that DealApplication is declared ZERO_PRODUCERS in pipeline-stage-registry.v1.json with evidence ("No .create() exists anywhere in the tree. submitDealApplication was deleted in FASE 1.2 with the entity at 0 rows") and the rule "Do not extend, do not project, do not resurrect." So this is an admin page over an entity with no producer and no rows, and its DealApplication.update write targets that entity. Retiring it is a deletion, not a migration, and needs the founder rather than a redirect.

invariants.note: Every workspace surface is a view+action on an existing host, so it is a LOGICAL route. This programme must not add a physical function.
invariants.no_direct_browser_crud: A workspace page must contain zero base44.entities writes. Reads through a governed portfolio call only.

redirect_semantics: ready=true means the redirect is LIVE in src/App.jsx. blocker_cleared=true means the technical obstacle is gone but the route still serves its own page, because section 2.5 requires parity, deep-link preservation and navigation tests before retirement, and section 24 puts that in C13. Conflating the two would let the registry claim a redirect that does not exist.

sidebar_cut.rule: Prompt section 2.5 forbids retiring a route before parity. Cutting the sidebar to 12 today would remove navigation to 10 pages that still exist and are reachable from nowhere else.
sidebar_cut.gate: dashboard:navigation:check fails if the sidebar is cut while any unmapped route still carries decision_required.
